title: Agentic reporting with fabio — headless Plan→Design→Author→Validate→Publish + Fabric IQ consumption
summary: How fabio delivers agent-native Power BI reporting: authoring reports from natural language through a Plan→Design→Author→Validate→Publish pipeline (the same shape as Microsoft's first-party Skills-for-Fabric Report Authoring skill, but headless/REST/CI — no Power BI Desktop or Desktop Bridge), and consuming data conversationally via data agents + ontologies (fabio's Fabric IQ analog). Explains the stage→command mapping, when to use fabio vs the Desktop-Bridge skill, PBIR schema conformance, and how to expose governed data for agents.
why_it_matters: In June 2026 Microsoft shipped first-party agent skills (github.com/microsoft/skills-for-fabric): a Power BI Report Authoring skill with a Plan→Design→Author→Validate→Publish pipeline, a Fabric IQ consumption skill (natural-language data answering in M365 Copilot/Cowork), and a Desktop Bridge. That skill 'currently only works with local PBIP files' and drives a running Power BI Desktop via the Desktop Bridge. fabio occupies the same agent-native space but is HEADLESS: it edits the PBIR definition over REST and publishes straight to a Fabric workspace, so it works in CI/CD, in containers, and against already-deployed items — no Desktop, no local PBIP required.

authoring_pipeline.Plan: Establish the data foundation + requirements. semantic-model list / list-tables / list-measures to pick the dataset and learn its real fields; report copilot-metadata to read an existing report's schema (pages, visuals, field bindings). Lock which model the report binds to and what questions each page answers.
authoring_pipeline.Design: Choose page archetypes and a visual per insight. context schema Report gives the PBIR structure; report add-visual --type enumerates valid visual types (card, clusteredBarChart, clusteredColumnChart, lineChart, pieChart, tableEx, slicer, textbox, …). Design to the published page/visual $schema.
authoring_pipeline.Author: report scaffold --spec builds a whole report from a compact {pages:[{visuals:[…]}]} JSON (data-bound visuals use category / measure(s) as Table.Column or Sum(Table.Column); textbox uses text). Incremental edits: add-page/add-visual/rename-page/set-active-page/delete-visual — a definition read-modify-write. --out writes the PBIR folder to disk for source control.
authoring_pipeline.Validate: report validate --source <folder> checks the PBIR (or PBIR-Legacy) definition against the schema BEFORE publishing; list-pages/list-visuals confirm bindings on a created report. Always validate before create/deploy.
authoring_pipeline.Publish: report create --definition <folder> --dataset pushes the validated PBIR to the workspace; report export renders PDF/PPTX/PNG; publish-to-web makes a public embed; deploy apply promotes across environments (see workflow cicd-deploy).

fabio_vs_skills_for_fabric.use_fabio_when: You want headless / CI-friendly authoring: publish straight to a workspace over REST, edit an ALREADY-DEPLOYED report, run in a pipeline/container, or script bulk report changes. No Power BI Desktop needed.
fabio_vs_skills_for_fabric.use_the_desktop_bridge_skill_when: You are interactively authoring LOCAL PBIP files in Power BI Desktop and want the edit→reload→screenshot loop the Desktop Bridge provides. fabio does not drive a Desktop session.
fabio_vs_skills_for_fabric.interop: Both target the SAME PBIR format, so a report authored locally with the MS skill can be published/managed by fabio and vice-versa. Keep reports in PBIR (not PBIR-Legacy) for agent-authorability and forward compatibility.

fabric_iq_consumption: The reporting counterpart to authoring is CONSUMPTION — chat-with-your-data. Microsoft's Fabric IQ consumption skill answers data questions from Power BI models across M365 Copilot/Cowork. fabio's native analog is the data-agent + ontology stack: data-agent add-datasource (Lakehouse/Warehouse/SQLDatabase/MirroredDatabase for NL2SQL, or SemanticModel for NL2DAX) → select-tables → publish → data-agent mcp-url gives a consumption/MCP endpoint agents can call; ontology graph-query grounds answers in a knowledge graph. This exposes governed Fabric data for any agent surface (fabio itself is also an MCP server: fabio mcp).
pbir_notes: PBIR is Microsoft's documented, agent-authorable report format — each page/visual is its own $schema-bearing JSON — and it becomes the ONLY supported report format at GA. Conform to the published visual.json/page.json schemas, prefer PBIR over the single-file PBIR-Legacy, and run report validate before every create/deploy.
what_agents_should_do: For 'build me a report / dashboard', run the Plan→Design→Author→Validate→Publish pipeline (workflow report-authoring): pick the dataset, design to the PBIR schema, scaffold or add-visual, validate, then create/publish.
Bind every data visual to REAL fields from the target semantic model (list-tables/list-measures first); a placeholder dataset id yields PowerBIEntityNotFound.
Prefer fabio for headless/CI/already-deployed reports; point users to the Desktop-Bridge skill only for interactive local-PBIP authoring.
For chat-with-your-data requests, route to the data-agent (+ ontology) consumption path rather than authoring a report.
